newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes weak on month-end dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes weak on month-end dlr demand.

text.p: The Mexican peso ceded more ground to the dollar towards the close on Monday on heightened month-end corporate demand for dollars and further increases in U.S. long bond yields, traders said.
"Corporate month-end demand and the lack of liquidity in the absence of continued dollar inflows made the peso weaken to close at more than 7.83 per dollar," a dealer said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 2.25 and 2.2 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.8370/7.8400 and 7.8320/7.8370 per dollar.
Yields on 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds climbed to 6.94 percent, up from 6.89 percent on Friday.
Traders had previously situated support for the 48-hour peso at 7.83 per dollar and said support was now at 7.85 pesos per dollar.
"The market is consolidating at this level. I don't think the peso will weaken further," one trader said.
Same-day peso contracts had closed earlier 1.7 centavos weaker at 7.8230/7.8250 per dollar.
